How small can a 78-billion parameter model get before it runs efficiently on a single GPU?

The focus of open-source AI development is shifting rapidly toward hardware efficiency, developer-centric agent tooling, and domain-specific engineering.

💻 Aleph Alpha released Kolibri, a 78.1B-parameter English-German Mixture-of-Experts model that activates just 3.46B parameters per token. It features a 1M-token context window, per-request reasoning effort, and Apache 2.0 FP8 weights that run on a single B200 or H200 GPU.

⚙️ DeepSeek launched official macOS and Windows desktop apps for DeepSeek Harness v0.2, its MIT-licensed agent harness. The preview release introduces a plugin manager, file and code-change review, and scheduled Automation Tasks, while supporting non-DeepSeek models via OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

🌐 The market is moving away from building redundant foundational models. Industry perspectives from InMobi and Glance highlight that the next phase of growth lies in model engineering and building domain-expert applications that the entire world will run on, rather than trying to build another ChatGPT.

As a developer, seeing highly capable models run on single-chip setups and agent harnesses transition to local desktop applications shows how fast the local developer ecosystem is maturing.

Are you prioritizing local agent workflows this year, or are you still heavily reliant on cloud-hosted APIs?
